state_background_check.value: No — Illinois's constitutional felony bar applies only to "an office created by this Constitution" (Illinois state and local offices) by its own text, not federal office; separately, the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates either way
state_background_check.snippet: Ill. Const. art. XIII, § 1: "A person convicted of a felony, bribery, perjury or other infamous crime shall be ineligible to hold an office created by this Constitution. Eligibility may be restored as provided by law." Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

bio_summary.value: Sean Casten represents Illinois’ 6th Congressional District located in the Chicago suburbs. Sean is committed to building a brighter, more affordable, and sustainable future. Since taking office, he has introduced and co-sponsored legislation in support of lowering costs, creating jobs, affirming women’s rights, protecting our seniors, and advocating for clean energy.

college.snippet: She is a graduate of the University of Chicago School of Economics and has an MBA in Healthcare Administration from George Washington University in WDC.

marital_status.snippet: Niki is a proud single-mother and life-long resident of the western suburbs of Chicago.

employment_record.value: Energy Consultant; worked in healthcare on the administration side of large health systems for 12 years; owned her own staffing business
employment_record.snippet: Today she is an Energy Consultant. She understands that energy is the foundation of a healthy economy. During the previous 12 years, Niki worked in healthcare on the administration side of large health systems. She knows how to deliver healthcare and what it takes to bend the cost curve. While there, she wrote corporate policy that impacted all segments of the population – from high-income to low-income populations, and rural and urban areas. She knows how to write meaningful policy. Prior to her time in healthcare, Niki owned her own staffing business and understands the challenges small business owners face.

platform.value: Push for real reform that will increase transparency in billing to foster competition among healthcare systems. Consumers should have more options in the marketplace and their policies should be transportable across state lines.
platform.snippet: Having worked in the healthcare industry, I will push for real reform that will increase transparency in billing, which will foster competition among healthcare systems. I also believe consumers should have more options in the marketplace and their policies should be transportable across state lines.

platform.value: Opposed to raising the Debt Ceiling. Will push to curb spending and limit the debt.
platform.snippet: I am opposed to raising the Debt Ceiling. It will only add to the already enormous burden we are placing on our children and grandchildren. I will push to curb spending and limit the debt we, as a Nation, incur.

platform.value: Oppose releasing violent felons on their own recognizance that the Safe-T Act requires. Support sensible criminal justice reforms, improved police training, and procedural improvements.
platform.snippet: I oppose releasing violent felons on their own recognizance that the Safe-T Act requires. The radical, left-wing agenda of attacking our police has deterred people from wanting to be policemen – and recruitment is at all-time lows. This only exacerbates the problems of keeping our communities safe. Sensible criminal justice reforms, improved police training, and procedural improvements are initiatives we can all get behind, and ones that I will support.
